text: {"claims":[{"id":"c4","evidence":[{"sid":"P2.S2","rel":"entails"},{"sid":"P2.S5","rel":"entails"}],"check":null,"reasoning":"P2.S2 says transactions over about 100 MB favor rollback journal modes; P2.S5 sets 3.11.0 as when WAL became as efficient for large transactions, supporting the before-3.11.0 qualifier."},{"id":"c7","evidence":[{"sid":"P8.S0","rel":"entails","sub":"as long as the locking_mode is set to EXCLUSIVE before the first attempted access"}],"check":null,"reasoning":"P8.S0 directly conditions using WAL without shared memory on setting locking_mode to EXCLUSIVE before the first attempted access."},{"id":"c9","evidence":[{"sid":"P9.S2","rel":"refutes","sub":"prior to version 3.7.0"},{"sid":"P8.S0","rel":"refutes","sub":"Beginning in SQLite version 3.7.4"}],"check":{"kind":"version","left":"3.22.0","op":">=","right":"3.7.0"},"reasoning":"P9.S2 ties the file-format error prevention to versions prior to 3.7.0, and P8.S0 says 3.7.4+ can use WAL, so the claimed 3.22.0 cutoff is too broad."}]}
